Mainly a note for a possible homebrew setting. The idea is to adopt a spell point system with regeneration. Characters will only be able to maintain a certain number of spells at any given time. A novice caster would have the ability to maintain 1 spell, more advanced casters would be able to maintain 2 or 3 spells, while the most dedicated casters would be able to maintain 4 or more spells.

Main issue with d20 buffs is the duration and stackability. Support casters can cast a myriad of duration based spells and not be fully taxed. For example in 3.5 if we know we are assaulting a fortress the cleric and wizard can mass spam Bear's Endurance, Bull's Strength, Greater Invisibility, etc. and give the party several minutes of Godliness.

I like the idea of a caster needing to maintain longer duration spells. Perhaps not via concentration checks but with spell points. If the casters choose to apply a Buff Over Time spell their magic should be drained until they cancel the spell.

Buff/Enchant/Manipulate/Etc. spells or other extended duration spells reduce available magic. If cast using your magic points they will reduce total magic available.

  • Ex. It costs 10MP to cast an aura. As long as the character maintains the aura their maximum magic is reduce by 10MP.
  • Ex. It costs 25MP to cast revive. As long as the character maintains the spell their maximum magic is reduced by 25MP. If they cease casting the person they have revived will die. The character can permanently Revive another person by using...
  • Ex. It costs 15MP to create and maintain a construct. As long as the character maintains the construct and it is not destroyed their maximum magic is reduced by 25MP. <Should it be possible to create a construct with its own magic pool, possibly in excess of xMP?>

Sharty has 100MP. Before the next wave of enemies Sharty casts; an aura to increase the AP of allies within 15', revives a dead guardsman, and animates a suit of armor. Sharty's maximum MP is limited to 50MP so long as the spells are maintained. During the attack two additional guards die defending the town gates. Sharty, a badass who is able to maintain 5 spells, revives both.

As the smoke clears Sharty has the sobering experience of telling the guardsmen that they cannot be maintained. They are given an hour to say their goodbyes to those they love or make peace with their enemies.

The idea that a revive spell is not permanent would dramatically change tone of a campaign. The ethical issue of raising a dead friend would take on a whole new light.

  • What happens when the party cleric has revived all fellow party members, has no additional MP remaining, and is slowly bleeding to death? The cleric will have to choose which party member to release.
  • If you revive an NPC how long are you bound to maintain the spell?
  • If you knew you could revive a child but would forever be burdened with their life, would you?
  • Would you assassinate a king, reanimate them, and use the threat of release to rule from the shadows?
  • A player (or their spouse) was revived by a wandering caster. They receive a note threatening the caster's life if they do not steal jewels. What do they do?
  • The caster who revived you is mortally wounded. They have maintained the spell for years and ask you search for a cure to their poison.
  • Are those who have been revived entitled to the same rights?
